title: Gift Exchange versus Monetary Exchange: Theory and Evidence

original_source.version_note: Complete original abstract only; full body inaccessible through attempted publisher/author routes.

central_claims: Money improves realized welfare relative to nonmonetary gift exchange by coordinating participants, despite theoretically better gift-exchange equilibria.

source_manifest.title: Gift Exchange versus Monetary Exchange: Theory and Evidence
source_manifest.finding: Original central claims were recorded before follow-up grading.

source_manifest.title: Camerer et al. Evaluating replicability of laboratory experiments in economics — Supplement, Tables S1–S2
source_manifest.finding: The preregistered independent comparison tests whether money raises efficiency over no money in six-person Lagos–Wright economies; replication N=96, original focal N=54, p=.674. The project only retested one selected result per paper.

source_manifest.title: Heterogeneous beliefs and trading inefficiencies
source_manifest.finding: Branch and McGough build a heterogeneous-beliefs monetary model and compare simulations with Duffy–Puzzello original experimental data, including rejections and trade patterns.

source_manifest.title: Evaluating replicability of laboratory experiments in economics: supplementary materials, Tables S1–S2
source_manifest.finding: The six-person money-versus-no-money welfare contrast did not replicate: N=96, p=.674, r=-.12, versus original N=54 and r=.76. This directly concerns the selected welfare comparison, not every theoretical result.

source_manifest.title: On the monetary exchange with multiple equilibrium money holdings distributions: An experimental approach
source_manifest.finding: Kamiya, Kobayashi, Shichijo and Shimizu study a different divisible-money model, compare its outcomes with Duffy/Puzzello, and report rare gift giving and efficient endogenous monetary exchange. Read publisher abstract, introduction and section text available through search indexing; direct retrieval was blocked.

search_gaps: This is a complete but selected cohort of laboratory economics experiments, not a representative sample of research success.
The replication project tests only one selected comparison, not every claim or the entire theoretical contribution.
Outcome review prioritizes independently tested validation; absent adoption/utility evidence remains unknown.
Original assessment uses its complete abstract only; attempted full-text publisher/author routes were inaccessible. No fabricated full-text reading.
Two independent grades adjudicated; six-paper repeat sample is not a population reliability estimate.
research.summary: The selected money-versus-no-money welfare advantage did not survive the 2016 independent test. Its experimental observations nevertheless became inputs and benchmarks for an independent monetary-theory extension. Blind repeat research added sources and corrected claim scope; initial and repeat grades remain archived.
